sources.fullCitation: Jacques Lefebvre. “Une excuse de moins: la France a l’un des plus beaux studios du monde.” Pour Vous, no. 9, 17 January 1929, p. 4. Bibliothèque numérique de la Cinémathèque de Toulouse, Pour Vous N0009. Article and images also reproduced by La Belle Équipe.

La Belle Équipe provides a convenient page-level reproduction and transcription of the article; it is treated as an access copy, not as the holding institution.

media.title: Joinville Studios — soundstage and lighting grid, 1929
media.description: Interior view of the Société des Cinéromans studios at Joinville-le-Pont, showing the steel roof structure, suspended projectors and overhead lighting equipment. The photograph accompanied Jacques Lefebvre’s industrial report on the Joinville complex in Pour Vous in January 1929.
media.altText: Sepia press photograph of a large film soundstage at Joinville-le-Pont, with steel roof trusses, catwalks and numerous suspended studio lights.
media.publicCaption: Interior of the Cinéromans studios at Joinville-le-Pont, with the overhead lighting grid and suspended projectors, January 1929.
media.publicCreditLine: Anonymous press photograph, Pour Vous, no. 9, 17 January 1929, p. 4; reproduced by La Belle Équipe, which credits the source copy to the Bibliothèque numérique de la Cinémathèque de Toulouse.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published without a photographer’s credit in France in 1929. The applicable terms for an anonymous published work have expired in France, the European Union and the United States. Reassess if the photographer is subsequently identified.
